summary: CRACKED the FORCE/PICK/EXIT door menu. KEY CORRECTION TO PRIOR SPIKES: FUN_0000_9345 (currently MISLABELED 'save_load_menu' in Ghidra) IS the door FORCE/PICK/EXIT menu, NOT a save/load UI. It is reached from FUN_0000_95ba's TYPE-7 special-record branch (call 0x92ea->0x9345 at file 0x9603), and the type-7 record is the door. (0x95ba's type-3 branch is the chest -> 0x9532, confirmed.) The OPEN command path is: dungeon main loop -> dungeon_in_camp_menu (0x2794) PARTY OPTIONS grid -> grid index 4 (case handler 0x294b) -> call FUN_0000_95ba -> for the special record AT THE PARTY CELL, type 7 -> call FUN_0000_9345 (door menu). The menu shows FORCE/PICK/EXIT (indexedMessage ids 0x834/0x835/0x836) via menu_grid_select (0x1574) at file 0x947f. FORCE (case 0) calls FUN_0000_8974; PICK (case 1) calls FUN_0000_8e4f (both currently mislabeled rest_save/load_session). Both first prompt WHO WILL TRY? (indexedMsg id 0x83e) via the member picker 0x9c8 + party_check_member_alive (0x2086), then run an animated strain/tumble bar, roll vs the door's lock field, and print success(0x841)/failure(0x842)/jammed(0x843). On success they open the door by clearing the special-record's +0x240 wall-plane bit for the current facing (FUN_0000_88af) -- they do NOT auto-step the party through. The +0x834..+0x843 ids map exactly to the task's indexedMessages 534..542 (FORCE..jammed), proving the identity.

findings.claim: OPEN is PARTY OPTIONS grid index 4 (column-major label OPEN per the prompt's record map). dungeon_in_camp_menu (0x2794) dispatches index 4 to case handler file 0x294b: call FUN_0000_95ba then status_effects_decay_timers(1) (advance a turn) then menu teardown. (The earlier maze-open-command.json claim that OPEN==index 0/0x876e is WRONG; 0x876e is the emblem-gate examiner. 0x95ba is OPEN.)

evidence.details: Jump table at file 0x2993 (jmp word [cs:bx+0x6ef7], delta 0x4564): entry 4 = CS 0x6eaf -> file 0x294b. file 0x294b: E86C6C = call 0x95ba; 0x294e mov ax,1; push; 0x2952 call 0x1053 (status_effects_decay_timers); 0x2956 jmp 0x29b2.

findings.claim: DOOR DETECTION: FUN_0000_95ba (file 0x95ba) finds the special-square record at the PARTY's OWN cell (z=*0x4f9c,y=*0x4f9e,x=*0x4fa0) via FUN_0000_366e, then branches on the record's TYPE byte at maze-table+0x360[recidx]: type 3 -> chest (call encounter_check_face_match 0x9532); type 7 -> DOOR (the type-7 branch additionally checks the +0x240 wall-plane orientation via getbit_chunk(0xe3fe) for the current facing == 1 OR == 2, and only then calls FUN_0000_9345 = the FORCE/PICK menu). So a forceable/pickable door is a TYPE-7 special record whose +0x240 facing-edge code is 1 or 2 at the party cell. NOTE: 0x95ba operates on the AT-FEET / current cell record (loop over records matching party x/y/z), the same record machinery as chests; the door-vs-chest distinction is purely the type byte (3 vs 7).

evidence.details: 0x95c1..0x95e1 get special-index byte at cell (+0x6c0) and call FUN_0000_366e(specialIdx,z,y,x)->recidx into [bp-2] (0xffff = none). 0x95f8 cmp [0x4fa8+si+0x360],3 (type3 chest -> 0x9600 call 0x9532). 0x9615 cmp [0x4fa8+si+0x360],7 (type7 door). For type7: 0x961c push 2; push *0x4f9a(facing)<<0; push +0x240[recidx]; call 0xe3fe (getbit_chunk width2); 0x9632 cmp ax,1 jz 0x965b; else repeat getbit_chunk with [bp-2] idx and cmp ax,2 jnz 0x9664. On match -> 0x965b push [bp-2]; 0x9603(after) call 0x92ea (FUN_0000_9345 prologue stub; 0x9345 body).

findings.recommend_check: Live: stand party facing a real graphic door (not the edge-3 stone arches that no-op), RETURN->OPEN (grid index 4), bp at 0x9615; confirm the type byte == 7 and that the +0x240 facing code is 1 or 2, then that 0x9345 is entered and the FORCE/PICK window appears. Also confirm 366e's specialIdx source (+0x6c0[z] vs per-cell).

findings.claim: FUN_0000_9345 (file 0x9345, MISLABELED 'save_load_menu') IS the FORCE/PICK/EXIT door menu. It opens a window (ui_window_create 0xbbb6 at 0x93ee, 5x19 cells at row -4), draws the PARTY OPTIONS header (msg id 0x7d2 via 0xc2db at 0x9442/0x944e), builds a 3-entry label list, and calls menu_grid_select (0x1574) at file 0x947f with label-base id 0x834 -> FORCE(0x834)/PICK(0x835)/EXIT(0x836) = the task's indexedMessages 534/535/536. The returned grid index dispatches: 0 -> FORCE path (0x948b), 1 -> PICK path (0x94c1), other -> exit. The menu is a single horizontal row of 3 (rows arg=1, cols arg=7 in the 0x947f call frame, mask local [bp-0x1a] with 3 entries set).

evidence.details: 0x9442 mov ax,0x12; push; push *0x3342; mov ax,0x7d2; push; call 0xc2db (draw header msg 0x7d2 = 'PARTY OPTIONS'/party_options=296). 0x9463..0x947c: push 0,5,1,7,1,push,&[bp-0x1a],mov ax,0x834;push, push window; 0x947f E8F280 = call 0x1574 (menu_grid_select). result -> [bp-0x1c]. 0x94f7 cmp ax,0 jz 0x948b(FORCE); 0x94fc cmp ax,1 jz 0x94c1(PICK). indexedMessages: id 0x834='FORCE'(534), 0x835='PICK'(535), 0x836='EXIT'(536), 0x83e='who_will_try}'(537) -- verified in extracted/messages/msg.json.

findings.claim: WHO WILL TRY? (indexedMsg id 0x83e = 537): BOTH FORCE and PICK invoke the member picker before rolling. FUN_0000_9345 case 0 (FORCE) at 0x948b: push 1; push 0x83e; call 0x9c8 (the picker/prompt fn) -> member index in [bp-4]; if != 0xffff: call party_check_member_alive(0x2086) -> if alive (nonzero) call FUN_0000_8974(member,recidx); on a 0 return re-prompt. PICK case 1 (0x94c1): identical but calls FUN_0000_8e4f. So the picker is gated by party_check_member_alive (0x2086); the chosen member must pass that liveness/consciousness check (0x2086 reads the member's status -- prior naming 'party_check_member_alive').

evidence.details: 0x948b mov ax,1;push; mov ax,0x83e;push; call 0x9c8; [bp-4]=ax; 0x949c cmp ax,0xffff jz exit; 0x94a1 push ax; call 0x2086 (party_check_member_alive); test ax; jz exit; 0x94aa push [bp+4](recidx); push [bp-4](member); call 0x8974 (FORCE); if ret nonzero set [bp-0x1c]=2 (done). 0x94c1 same with 0x83e + call 0x8e4f (PICK).

findings.claim: FORCE (FUN_0000_8974): args (member [bp+4], recidx [bp+6]). Reads door LOCK field = getbit_chunk(0xe3fe, width=5, off=0) of the record's +0x630 byte -> [bp-8] (lock strength, 5-bit 0..31). Reads member char struct (member*0x1b0): STR-like stat at +0x4514 (struct-rel 0x110). STRAIN-BAR LENGTH [bp-0x38] = clamp(0x12 - (stat - lock) + lock, 1..0x12); forced to 0x12 if door is jammed ([bp-0x3c], set when +0x240 facing code == 2). The ROLL [bp-6] = idiv32( char+0x4404 (current stamina/HP) * 100 , char+0x4406 (max) ) then * (char+0x4514 stat) / 100 (two 0xf9ba signed-32 divides). The SUCCESS test: outcome[bp-0x36] = (strain progress [bp-0x3a] < strain length [bp-0x38]) ? 1 : 0; if jammed-flag set, outcome forced to 2. Message printed = 0x841 + outcome (0x841 success=540 / 0x842 failure=541 / 0x843 jammed=542). RNG = rng_next thunk 0xc47e (wroot 0x9e2, returns 0..N-1) used at several decision points (c47e(0x32), c47e(6), c47e(3)). Animation string = 0x840 ('straining..press_~' = 539).

evidence.details: 0x8af2 push 5;push 0;push [bp-4](+0x630 byte);call 0xe3fe -> [bp-8] lock. 0x8b1d push 2; push *0x4f9a; push +0x240[recidx]; call 0xe3fe; 0x8b30 cmp ax,2; jnz; mov [bp-0x3c],1 (jammed). 0x8b3e mov ax,0x840; call 0xc1f7 (load 'straining' string). 0x8b6c imul [bp+4],0x1b0; mov al,[bx+0x4514](stat); sub [bp-8](lock); ax=0x12 - that; add [bp-8]; -> [bp-0x38] strain len; clamp 1..0x12; if jammed -> 0x12. 0x8bfa: ax=[bx+0x4404]*100; idiv32(0xf9ba) by [bx+0x4406]; * [bx+0x4514]; /100 (0xf9ba) -> [bp-6] roll. 0x8da0: ax=1; cmp [bp-0x3a],[bp-0x38]; jl -> ax=0; [bp-0x36]=ax. 0x8db1 if [bp-0x3c]!=0 -> [bp-0x36]=2. 0x8df0 ax=[bp-0x36]+0x841; load+draw msg.

findings.recommend_check: Live: bp at 0x8b6c and 0x8da0; FORCE a known door with a high-STR vs low-STR member and read [bp-8](lock), [bx+0x4514](stat), [bp-0x38](strain len), [bp-0x3a](progress), [bp-6](roll), [bp-0x36](outcome). The strain-bar formula and the success comparator (JL at 0x8da9) are the load-bearing claims and are easy to misread statically -- confirm direction and confirm whether the roll [bp-6] or the strain-len comparison decides success (both appear; the visible success/fail message is driven by [bp-0x36] which is the JL comparison).

findings.claim: PICK (FUN_0000_8e4f): args same as FORCE. Reads door lock field = getbit_chunk(width=5,off=0) of +0x630 -> [bp-8]. Reads member skill: char+0x440c (struct-rel 0x8) + char+0x452b (struct-rel 0x127) -> [bp-6], clamped to <=0x5f. TUMBLER count [bp-0x44] = (lock[bp-8] / 3) + 1, clamped <=6. If door +0x240 facing code == 2 (jammed/welded), it picks a specific tumbler index (0x4fa4+0x4fa2 mod tumblers) and force-fails it ([bx+0x5234]=0x64, [bp-0x46]=1). Animation string = 0x83f ('tumbling..press_~' = 538). Per-tumbler it rolls rng_next(0xc47e)([bp-6]) and resolves via 0xc041 (draw-number/compare). On overall SUCCESS ([bp-0x36]==1) it checks member class char+0x4587 (== 3 || 6 || 0xd, the thief-ish classes) and if so awards skill via FUN_0000_54c0(0xf,member), then RNG c47e(3) -> call FUN_0000_88af (open door). Outcome message = 0x841 + outcome (success/failure/jammed). So PICK uses a PICK-LOCKS SKILL (char+0x440c base + char+0x452b modifier), NOT raw Agility, vs the same +0x630 5-bit lock field.

evidence.details: 0x9093 imul [bp+4],0x1b0; mov ax,[bx+0x440c]; add al,[bx+0x452b] -> [bp-6]; cmp 0x5f clamp. 0x90b8 [bp-8]/3; inc -> [bp-0x44] tumblers; clamp 6. 0x90df push 2;push *0x4f9a; push +0x240[recidx]; call 0xe3fe; cmp 2 -> jam path 0x90fe: (0x4fa4+0x4fa2) mod [bp-0x44]; [bx+0x5234]=0x64; [bp-0x46]=1. 0x911e mov ax,0x83f; call 0xc1f7. 0x9171 push [bp-6]; call 0xc47e (rng). outcome dispatch 0x9258: cmp [bp-0x36],0 jz fail(0x891d); cmp 1: 0x926c mov al,[bx+0x4587](class) cmp 3/6/0xd -> call 0x54c0(0xf,member) skill-up; 0x9291 call 0xc47e(3); call 0x88af(open). 0x92e7 ax=[bp-0x36]+0x841 message.

findings.recommend_check: Live: bp 0x9093 and 0x9258; PICK a door with a thief vs non-thief member; read [bx+0x440c]/[bx+0x452b] (skill components), [bp-8](lock), [bp-0x44](tumblers), [bp-0x36](outcome), [bx+0x4587](class). Confirm the +0x440c/+0x452b struct fields are the PICK-LOCKS skill (cross-check vs wpcvw skill struct: wpcvw-skill-action.json reads skill level at +0x451c and class at +0x4587). Confirm whether +0x440c is current-skill and +0x452b a bonus, or vice-versa.

findings.claim: OUTCOMES are a single code [bp-0x36] in BOTH FORCE and PICK: 0=FAILURE (msg 0x842=541), 1=SUCCESS (0x841=540), 2=JAMMED (0x843=542). The message is uniformly msg-id (0x841 + outcome). JAMMED is NOT a botched-FORCE-ruins-PICK state machine: it is a PRE-EXISTING door condition detected the same way in both handlers -- the door's +0x240 wall-plane facing code == 2 (read via getbit_chunk width2 at the current facing). When that holds, FORCE sets [bp-0x3c]=1 (forcing strain to max and outcome to 2) and PICK sets [bp-0x46]=1 (force-fail a tumbler) -> outcome 2. So a code-2 door is welded/jammed and neither FORCE nor PICK can open it; there is no separate persistent 'I jammed it' bit written by a failed attempt that this code inspects. (Open is encoded as the +0x240 facing code being cleared to the open value; jam=2 is just one of those edge codes.)

evidence.details: FORCE 0x8db1 cmp [bp-0x3c],0 jz; else mov [bp-0x36],2. jam flag [bp-0x3c] set at 0x8b35 when +0x240 facing code==2. PICK jam path 0x90fc..0x9115 (cmp ax,2; [bp-0x46]=1). Both: msg = [bp-0x36]+0x841 (0x841/0x842/0x843). No setbits write to a 'jammed' persistent bit appears in 0x8974/0x8e4f outside the success door-open path.

findings.recommend_check: Live: try to FORCE then PICK the SAME door across attempts and watch for any persisted state that makes a 2nd attempt behave differently (e.g. does a failed FORCE write +0x630 or +0x240 to mark it jammed?). Confirm what +0x240 facing code value means 'open' vs 'jammed(2)' vs 'closed(1)'. The jammed==pre-existing claim assumes no failed-attempt writeback; verify no setbits on +0x240/+0x630 happens on the FAILURE branch (0x891d).

findings.claim: DOOR-OPEN ON SUCCESS does NOT call door_set (FUN_0000_6d62) and does NOT auto-step the party. Both FORCE and PICK, on success, call FUN_0000_88af(recidx): it edits the special-record's +0x240 wall-plane bitfield directly -- CLEARS the bit at [facing] (facing/8 byte, facing%8 mask, AND ~mask) and SETS the bit at [facing+1] (the adjacent/back orientation). That opens the door in the record's wall plane. The FAILURE branch calls FUN_0000_891d(recidx) instead: it clears a per-facing word [0x4ee0+facing*2]=0, calls FUN_0000_84ce (record-update) and plays sound 4 (0xc546). After both, control returns to FUN_0000_9345 which (on the 'done'=2 path) tears down the window. The party is left standing in front of the now-open door; movement is a separate subsequent input. (NOTE: this differs from the emblem-gate path 0x850e which DOES call door_set 0x6d62 + setbits +0x60/+0x120 -- doors via FORCE/PICK use the lighter +0x240-only edit in 0x88af.)

evidence.details: FORCE success 0x8dce push [bp+6]; call 0x88af. PICK success 0x9299 push [bp+6]; call 0x88af. 0x88af: ax=[0x4fa8]+recidx*1+0x240 -> [bp-4]; f=*0x4f9a; idiv 8 -> si=f/8; al=[bx+si]; clear bit (1<<(f%8)) AND ~ ; store; then f+1: set bit (1<<((f+1)%8)) OR; store. No call to 0x6d62. 0x891d (failure): [bx+0x4ee0(f<<1)]=0; call 0x84ce; play sound 0xc546(4).

findings.recommend_check: Live: bp 0x88af; successfully FORCE/PICK a door; read +0x240 record bits before/after and confirm the forward edge clears (door becomes passable to maze_can_step_in_facing) and that NO automatic step occurs (party x/y/z unchanged until next move key). Confirm whether 0x88af alone makes the door renderable-as-open, or whether a re-render/door_set is also needed (0x891d plays the open sound on FAILURE which is suspicious -- verify the success vs failure sound mapping live).

findings.claim: TURN COST: OPEN consumes one status-effect tick regardless of door outcome -- the case handler at 0x294b calls status_effects_decay_timers(1) (0x1053) after FUN_0000_95ba returns. ANIMATION: the straining(FORCE 0x840)/tumbling(PICK 0x83f) effect IS a real interactive loop, not a single printed line. FORCE loops [bp-0x38] (strain length) iterations drawing char 0x61 ('a') via 0xdd53 building a progress bar, polling the keyboard each frame (kbd thunk 0xe0df / 0xe1c0; ENTER 0x0d cancels). PICK loops per-tumbler ([bp-0x44] tumblers) drawing/animating each lock pin via 0xc041 and rng_next. SOUND: the open/result sound is play_sound thunk 0xc546(4) (sound index 4) -- played in 0x891d (failure path) and likely the success path; FORCE/PICK do not appear to use a distinct per-outcome sound index beyond 4 in these handlers.

evidence.details: Turn: 0x294e mov ax,1; call 0x1053. FORCE bar: 0x8bc4..0x8be5 loop [bp-2] < [bp-0x38]: push 0xc; push 0x61; call 0xdd53 (draw char). 0x8d77 call 0xe0df (kbd check); 0x8d83 call 0xe1c0; cmp al,0xd (ENTER abort). PICK tumbler loop 0x9169..(jmp 0x9212): per [bp-2]<tumblers rng_next(0xc47e) + 0xc041 draw/compare. Sound 0xc546(4) at 0x8946 (in 0x891d failure).

findings.recommend_check: Live: confirm the strain/tumble bar animates frame-by-frame and is interruptible by ENTER, and capture the actual sound index(es) played on success vs failure vs jammed (set bp at 0xc546 sites). Wall-clock timing should be tuned by feel per CLAUDE.md, not matched to DOSBox.

findings.claim: CORRECTION TO maze-open-command.json: that spike concluded 'there is NO FORCE/PICK/KEY submenu in wmaze' and dismissed FUN_0000_9345 as save_load_menu and 0x95ba's type-7 branch as a 'save-crystal/cabin special'. Both are WRONG. FUN_0000_9345 is the FORCE/PICK/EXIT door menu (proven by its use of indexedMessage ids 0x834/0x835/0x836=FORCE/PICK/EXIT and 0x83e=WHO WILL TRY, and animation strings 0x83f/0x840 and outcome strings 0x841/0x842/0x843). The spike's grep for FORCE/PICK in the msg.json *records* table missed them because these strings live in the indexedMessages table (ids 0x834..0x843 = entries 534..542), accessed via the indexed-string loader (0xc1f7 for menu labels, 0x9c8 for the WHO picker), not the record-message loader. NOTE on KEY: the prompt/recollection mentions a third action USE A KEY; this 9345 menu only has FORCE/PICK/EXIT (3 labels at 0x834..0x836). A key-use is handled separately as OPTIONS USE ITEM (case index 3 -> *0x363a=0x14 -> wdopt), not as a 4th label here -- unless a different/larger door menu exists for keyed doors (not found in wmaze statically).

evidence.details: indexedMessages (extracted/messages/msg.json): entry534 id0x834 'FORCE', 535 0x835 'PICK', 536 0x836 'EXIT', 537 0x83e 'who_will_try}', 538 0x83f tumbling, 539 0x840 straining, 540 0x841 success, 541 0x842 failure, 542 0x843 jammed. FUN_0000_9345 references 0x834 (menu base, 0x947f), 0x83e (0x948b/0x94c1 picker). FUN_0000_8974/8e4f reference 0x840/0x83f (anim) and 0x841 (outcome base).

findings.claim: BLOCKER (methodology): the dynamic-trace plan for this pass (set an execution breakpoint at file 0x8b6c / 0x8da0 / 0x9093 / 0x9258 / 0x88af, single-step the JL at 0x8da9, and read stack locals [bp-8]/[bp-0x38]/[bp-0x3a]/[bp-6]/[bp-0x36]/[bp-0x44]) is NOT POSSIBLE with the MCP backend exposed to this session. The wiz6 MCP surfaced ONLY the DOSBox-X save-state tools; dosbox_set_breakpoint, dosbox_step, dosbox_step_over, dosbox_run_until, dosbox_resume, dosbox_pause, dosbox_clear_breakpoint, dosbox_get_call_chain are all explicitly [STUB] (their tool descriptions read: 'requires the Phase 9 dynamic-driving backend (node-pty + ncurses scraper OR DOSBox-X TCP debug-port patch)'). The dosbox_live_* frame-stepping tools (dosbox_live_step/key/read/find) that CLAUDE.md describes as the primary backend were NOT exposed to this session at all. Consequence: the load-bearing questions Q2 (FORCE success comparator + JL direction), Q3 (what fills strain-progress [bp-0x3a] — keypresses vs rng_next, the c47e(0x32)/(6)/(3) feeds), Q4 (PICK per-tumbler 0xc041 resolution + outcome rule), and the [bp-8] lock / [bp-0x36] outcome reads CANNOT be answered — they require halting the CPU INSIDE FUN_0000_8974/FUN_0000_8e4f, which a static save state cannot do. A save state is a single passive snapshot; reading transient BP-relative stack locals at a specific instruction is impossible without an execution breakpoint or single-step. These remain at their prior STATIC confidence (low) and were NOT upgraded.

findings.claim: COULD NOT locate the door's special-square record statically, so Q1 (the +0x630 lock value for this door) is UNRESOLVED. recidx is the return of FUN_0000_366e, computed transiently inside FUN_0000_95ba; with no execution breakpoint there is no way to capture it. Attempts to reconstruct the record-table addressing from the static notes failed/contradicted: (a) the word at DGROUP 0x4fa8 = 0x8184, and reading DGROUP+0x8184 returns all-zeros — so 0x8184 is a value/scalar, not a record-table base pointer; (b) treating 0x4fa8 as an array-label and reading the putative type-byte array at DGROUP+(0x4fa8+0x360)=0x5308 returns ASCII '0'/'1' bytes (0x30/0x31) with 0x00 separators — clearly string/name data, NOT a small-integer type array. findings.claim: RAW-ASM READ (ndisasm of wmaze.ovr, authoritative control-flow) CORRECTS three load-bearing errors in force-roll-formula/pick-roll-formula/outcomes-success-fail-jammed/door-open-on-success-88af. (1) OUTCOME POLARITY: msg printed = [bp-0x36]+0x841 (0x8df0/0x92xx), and 0x841=540='success', 0x842=541='failure', 0x843=542='jammed'. So outcome 0=SUCCESS, 1=FAILURE, 2=JAMMED (prior finding had 0=failure/1=success backwards). (2) FORCE SUCCESS RULE: at 0x8da0 ax=1; cx=progress[bp-0x3a]; cmp cx,strain_len[bp-0x38]; JL(0x8da9)->skip(ax stays 1=>outcome1=FAILURE); else ax=0=>outcome0=SUCCESS. I.e. SUCCESS iff progress>=strain_len (prior finding said progress<len=success, backwards). strain_len=clamp(0x12-STR+2*lock,1,0x12) (=0x12 if jammed); effSTR=STR*SPcur/SPmax (Spirit Points, NOT HP); progress=clamp(sum(4x rng_next(effSTR))/4,1,0x12); plus a ~1/50 (rng_next(50)==0) or effSTR<=0 fatigue branch draining SP. (3) ROUTINE ROLES SWAPPED: outcome 0 (SUCCESS) -> call 0x891d (clears 0x4ee0[facing], record-update 0x84ce, sound 4 => door opens); outcome 1/2 -> 1/3 (rng_next(3)==0) -> call 0x88af (flips +0x240 edge bits: clear bit[facing], set bit[facing+1] => advances the door toward the jammed/welded state). So a FAILED FORCE/PICK has a 1/3 chance to damage the door. PICK: skill=clamp(level[+0x440c]+skulduggery[+0x452b],<=0x5f); tumblers=clamp(lock/3+1,<=6); per-tumbler passes iff rng_next(skill)>difficulty[BSS 0x5234+i] (normal difficulty 0; jammed door forces one tumbler=0x64); SUCCESS iff all tumblers pass; a FAILED pick awards Skulduggery skill XP (call 0x54c0(0xf,member)) to classes 3/6/0xd before the 1/3 damage roll.
